references.text: In [ref:Joh 1:14|John 1:14], the Word is described as "full of grace and truth", and it is from this fullness (πλήρωμα) that believers have received, as verse 16 expresses.
[ref:Kol 1:19|Colossians 1:19] states that "all the fullness" (πλήρωμα) was God's will to dwell in Christ – the same fullness that John 1:16 says believers have partaken of.
[ref:Kol 2:9-10|Colossians 2:9-10] emphasizes that all the fullness of deity dwells bodily in Christ, and that believers have been filled in him – a parallel to receiving from his fullness.
[ref:Ef 1:7-8|Ephesians 1:7-8] describes the riches of grace given to us in Christ, a grace that overflows – something that corresponds with "grace upon grace" in John 1:16.
[ref:Ef 3:19|Ephesians 3:19] speaks of being filled with all the fullness (πλήρωμα) of God, paralleling the idea of receiving from Christ's fullness.
[ref:Ef 4:13|Ephesians 4:13] uses the expression "the measure of the fullness of Christ" as the goal for the maturity of believers – a continuation of the theme of partaking in his fullness.
[ref:Rom 5:17|Romans 5:17] speaks of receiving "the abundance of grace and the gift of righteousness", which reflects the overflowing grace in John 1:16.
[ref:Rom 5:20-21|Romans 5:20-21] describes how grace became even more abundant where sin increased – a grace that replaces and surpasses, parallel to "grace upon grace".
[ref:Joh 3:34|John 3:34] says that God gives the Spirit without measure to the Son, and it is from this unlimited fullness that believers receive part, as verse 16 expresses.

[ref:2 Mos 34:6|Exodus 34:6] proclaims the Lord's grace (חֶסֶד) as rich and overflowing – an Old Testament background for the grace that in John 1:16 is given in continually renewed fullness through Christ.

[ref:Sal 84:12|Psalm 84:12] says that the Lord gives grace and glory and withholds no good thing – an Old Testament testimony to God's generous grace, which finds its fulfillment in Christ (John 1:16).
[ref:Tit 3:4-6|Titus 3:4-6] describes how God's grace and kindness were richly poured out on us through Jesus Christ – an expression of the grace we have received from his fullness.
